I've written `ArrayUtilsAgentTest` at `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/ArrayUtilsAgentTest.java` (JUnit 5.14.3, matching the project), self-contained with no dependency on other test classes.

I covered: `clone`, `contains`/`containsAny`, `get`, `getComponentType`, `getDimensions`, `getLength` (including the non-array `IllegalArgumentException` case), `hashCode`, `indexesOf`, `indexOf`/`lastIndexOf` (including negative/overflowing `startIndex`, `NaN`, double tolerance, and `Object[]` type-mismatch cases), `isArrayIndexValid`, `isEmpty`/`isNotEmpty`, `isEquals`, `isSameLength`, `isSameType`, `isSorted` (primitive, natural-order, and `Comparator`), `nullToEmpty`/`nullTo`, `reverse` (full and ranged, with under/overflow bounds), `setAll`, `shift` (full and ranged, with modulo wraparound), `shuffle` (checked as a permutation), `startsWith`, `subarray`, `swap` (single and ranged, with overflow/negative indices), `toArray`, `toMap` (including malformed-entry errors), `toObject`/`toPrimitive` round-trips, `toPrimitive` with null handling and the NPE case, and `toString`/`toStringArray`.

All 40 tests pass against the current implementation — after extensive manual review of the `ArrayUtils` source (indexOf/lastIndexOf family, isSorted, swap/shift/reverse ranges, subarray, toPrimitive/toObject, nullToEmpty, toMap, etc.), I found no discrepancy between the documented/expected behavior and the actual code, so I'm not reporting any bugs for this class.
